rule: An other_fact (its English text) whose bge-m3 cosine similarity to one of a scheme's residual conditions is at least the threshold is attached to the match result and turns eligible into needs_checking. It never produces not_eligible.
pairs_source: Every (other_fact, residual_condition) pair for the dev split's rows with other_facts: their top-10 hybrid-retrieval candidates plus their target schemes. Profiles from understand-v4 (the pairs predate understand-v4.1). Split: dev only.
rationale: Similarity does not separate genuine touches from unrelated pairs. The reviewed genuine touches score 0.442-0.776, and unrelated pairs reach 0.650 ('I have a job' vs 'The applicant should be pregnant'). Any threshold lets through some unrelated pairs and misses some genuine ones, so the threshold only decides how many candidates are downgraded.

The rule can only turn eligible into needs_checking, never into not_eligible. Missing a genuine touch can leave a wrong 'eligible'; an unrelated touch costs only an extra check. So the threshold leans low.

0.48 sits just under 0.493, the genuine pair for gold_084's excluded scheme (three months of work vs a one-year membership rule). At 0.48, 72% of candidates with other_facts get at least one touch; at 0.45, 82%; at 0.40, 96%, where the rule would downgrade nearly everything.

The one genuine touch below the threshold is gold_014 (a retired government teacher vs PM-KISAN's exclusion of retired government employees, 0.442). Catching it needs a threshold of 0.442 or lower, which touches 86% of candidates.
caveat: The threshold was chosen with gold_084's score in view: it sits 0.013 under the genuine pair (0.493). So gold_084's dev result is fitted, not evidence that the rule works. The same scheme also has an unrelated pair at 0.499 (a marriage-card rule), which alone would downgrade it. Only rows the threshold was not chosen on can show whether it works.
